chunks.title: Frequently Asked Questions — Frequently Asked Questions [#frequently-asked-questions]
Steam Game Idler PRO — What is Steam Game Idler PRO? [#what-is-steam-game-idler-pro]
chunks.text:
What is Steam Game Idler PRO? [#what-is-steam-game-idler-pro] First and foremost, Steam Game Idler is completely free to use, and always will be. All of the core features of SGI are available to all users at no cost. Steam Game Idler **PRO** is an optional way to support the development of SGI. To thank you for your support, **PRO** subscribers receive a range of additional benefits that enhance the SGI experience. There are two subscription tiers available: **Casual** and **Gamer**, each unlocking a different set of benefits. By subscribing to **PRO**, you help with the ongoing development and maintenance of SGI, ensuring that it continues to improve and evolve over time. Every tier, **including Free**, has access to every core feature: * Card Farming * Achievement Unlocker * Achievement Manager * Inventory Manager * Playtime Booster * and so on.. PRO only unlocks the automation/convenience extras listed below | Feature | Free | Casual ($2/mo) | Gamer ($4/mo) | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----: | :------------: | :-----------: | | AI Assistant messages | 3/day | 25/day | 50/day | | Multi-account support via [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/multi-account) | 1 | 3 | 10 | | Unlock achievements for multiple games at once | 1 | 3 | 32 | | Ad-free experience | | | | | Exclusive themes | | | | | Custom background image | | | | | Custom fonts | | | | | Unique Discord chat role | | | | | Real-time live support | | | | | Automatic games list updates | | | | | Automatic Steam Credentials retrieval | | | | | Automatic free game redemption | | | | | Automatic card farming | | | | | Sell duplicate inventory items | | | | | Import achievement unlock timings | | | | | Custom Steam status while [signed in with Steam](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in) | | | |

\* Prices are in USD and exclude taxes. Billed monthly, cancel anytime.

chunks.title: Steam Game Idler PRO — FAQ [#faq]
chunks.text:
FAQ [#faq]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="How to Subscribe to PRO" id="how-to-subscribe">
    <Steps>
      <Step>
        Open Steam Game Idler
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Click the <MockButton type="go-pro" /> badge in the app's title bar
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Select your desired subscription tier *(Casual or Gamer)*
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Click <MockButton type="pay-stripe" /> or <MockButton type="pay-paypal" /> depending on your preferred payment method, then complete your purchase
      </Step>

      <Step>
        You will receive an email containing your **license key**
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Open Steam Game Idler, navigate to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />, paste your license key into the input field, and click <MockButton type="activate" />

        Your license key is tied to one device at a time. To transfer it to a new device, activate it on the new device and confirm the transfer when prompted.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How to Cancel PRO Subscription" id="how-to-cancel">
    <Steps>
      <Step>
        Open Steam Game Idler
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Navigate to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Click <MockButton type="manage-subscription" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Follow the prompts to confirm your cancellation
      </Step>
    </Steps>

    After cancellation, you will retain access to **PRO** benefits until the end of your current billing period.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Transferring to a New Device" id="transfer-device">
    Your license key is tied to one device at a time. To transfer it to a new device:

    <Steps>
      <Step>
        Open Steam Game Idler on your **new device**
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Navigate to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Enter your license key and click <MockButton type="activate" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        A prompt will appear asking you to confirm the transfer. Click <MockButton type="continue" />
      </Step>
    </Steps>

    Your subscription will immediately become active on the new device. The previous device will lose access on its next launch.

    If you reinstalled the app on the **same machine**, your key will activate without any transfer prompt as the device is recognised by its hardware ID.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Switch Between PRO Tiers" id="switch-tiers">
    To switch between **PRO** tiers, simply cancel your current subscription and subscribe to your desired tier following the standard subscription process.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Invoices and Receipts" id="invoices-receipts">
    After subscribing to Steam Game Idler **PRO**, you will receive an email receipt for your purchase. To view your billing history and upcoming invoices:

    <Steps>
      <Step>
        Open Steam Game Idler
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Navigate to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Click <MockButton type="manage-subscription" />
      </Step>

      <Step>
        Follow the prompts to view your billing history and invoices
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Refund Policy" id="refund-policy">
    As **PRO** subscriptions are a donation rather than a normal subscription service, they are generally non-refundable. However, refunds can be considered on a case-by-case basis.

    If there was a mistake, unexpected charge, or issue with your subscription, please use the in-app help desk to contact support or send an email to [contact@steamgameidler.com](mailto:contact@steamgameidler.com).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Fraudulent Chargebacks" id="fraudulent-chargebacks">
    Chargebacks are when a payment made on your credit card or bank account is reversed, typically when the customer disputes a charge or claims it was unauthorized.

    Steam Game Idler is a small independent project, and fraudulent chargebacks have a significant negative impact.

    If a chargeback is filed on your **PRO** subscription without prior communication, your access to Steam Game Idler and all of its features may be revoked permanently.

    If you believe a charge was made to your account in error, please contact support via the in-app help desk or send an email to [contact@steamgameidler.com](mailto:contact@steamgameidler.com).
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]
chunks.text:
Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]


This page covers common issues and their solutions when using Steam Game Idler.

<Callout type="info">
  Always check the [FAQ](/docs/faq) section first, as many common questions are answered there
</Callout>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Preliminary Checks [#preliminary-checks]
chunks.text:
Preliminary Checks [#preliminary-checks]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Check System Requirements [#check-system-requirements]

    * Windows 10/11 or Linux (64-bit)
    * Internet connection
    * Steam client installed and running (only required if you use [Legacy Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#legacy-sign-in), which is Windows-only — Linux supports Steam Sign-in only)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Verify Your Sign-In [#verify-your-sign-in]

    * If using [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in), make sure you completed any Steam Guard prompt fully
    * If using [Legacy Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#legacy-sign-in), make sure the Steam client is running and you're signed in to at least one account
    * Your Steam profile is set to public (required for some features regardless of sign-in method)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Check SGI Installation [#check-sgi-installation]

    * SGI is installed in the default location
    * You're running the latest version
    * Windows Defender/antivirus isn't blocking SGI
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Installation Issues [#installation-issues]
chunks.text:
Installation Issues [#installation-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="SGI won't install" id="install-fails">
    * Make sure you downloaded the installer from the official [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases) or [steamgameidler.com](https://steamgameidler.com). Files from other sources may be incomplete or modified
    * Right-click the installer and select **Run as administrator**
    * Temporarily disable your antivirus/Windows Defender during installation (see below), then re-enable it afterwards
    * Make sure you have enough free disk space
    * If the installer hangs or crashes, restart your PC and try again
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Antivirus or Windows Defender is blocking SGI" id="antivirus-blocking">
    SGI's installer and its bundled helper process (`SteamUtility.exe`, used for idling, achievement management, and Steam Sign-in) are not code-signed with a paid certificate, so Windows SmartScreen and some antivirus programs may flag them as "unknown publisher" or quarantine them. This is a false positive.

    If a feature fails immediately with **"The Steam agent component is missing from this installation."** or **"Couldn't start the Steam agent process."**, `SteamUtility.exe` has most likely been quarantined or deleted — follow the steps below.

    <Steps>
      <Step>
        ### If SmartScreen blocks the installer [#if-smartscreen-blocks-the-installer]

        Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### If your antivirus quarantines or deletes a file [#if-your-antivirus-quarantines-or-deletes-a-file]

        Restore the file from quarantine, then add an exclusion for SGI's install folder (default: `C:\Program Files\Steam Game Idler\`) and for `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\`
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### If a feature won't start because SteamUtility.exe is removed [#if-a-feature-wont-start-because-steamutilityexe-is-removed]

        Re-run the installer to restore the missing file, after adding the exclusion above
      </Step>
    </Steps>

    <Callout type="info">
      If you'd like to verify the source code yourself, SGI's source code is entirely public. See the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler)
    </Callout>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Missing .NET Framework / SteamUtility errors" id="dotnet-missing">
    SGI's idling, sign-in, and achievement features rely on a bundled helper process (`SteamUtility.exe`) which requires the **.NET Framework 4.8** runtime. Most Windows 10/11 installs already include this, but if idling, sign-in, or achievement actions fail immediately with no clear error:

    * Install the [.NET Framework 4.8 runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet-framework/net48) from Microsoft
    * Restart your PC after installing, then try again

    This is also a common cause of **"The Steam agent process closed unexpectedly."** or **"Steam took too long to respond. Please try again."** — both mean `SteamUtility.exe` stopped responding, which a missing runtime causes just as often as the antivirus case above.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I need admin rights to install or update SGI" id="admin-rights">
    SGI installs per-machine by default (available to all Windows users on the PC), which requires administrator privileges. If you don't have admin rights:

    * Ask an administrator to run the installer once
    * Updates are installed silently in the background and also require the original install permissions. If updates consistently fail, reinstall with an administrator account
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Startup Issues [#startup-issues]
chunks.text:
Startup Issues [#startup-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="SGI won't start/run at all" id="wont-start">
    <Steps>
      <Step>
        ### Check for a hidden window or tray icon [#check-for-a-hidden-window-or-tray-icon]

        SGI's main window is hidden until it finishes loading, and may also be set to start minimized. Look for the SGI icon in your system tray (bottom-right of the taskbar, click the **^** arrow to see hidden icons)
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Check for leftover processes [#check-for-leftover-processes]

        Open **Task Manager** and look for `steam-game-idler.exe` and `SteamUtility.exe`. If either is running but nothing appears, end both processes and relaunch SGI
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Check the log file [#check-the-log-file]

        If SGI ran before, open today's log file from <MockButton type="view-log-file" /> in [Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug) and check it for errors from the last session
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Reset window state [#reset-window-state]

        A corrupted window-position file can prevent the window from appearing. Close SGI completely (including via Task Manager), then delete `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\.window-state.json` (if present) and relaunch
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Reinstall [#reinstall]

        If none of the above works, uninstall SGI, restart your PC, and reinstall the latest version
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="SGI is open in the system tray but I can't see the main window" id="tray-no-window">
    This usually means **Start minimized to tray** is enabled, or the window was closed to tray and is simply hidden.

    * **Left-click** the SGI icon in the system tray to show and focus the main window
    * If clicking the tray icon does nothing, right-click it and select **Show**
    * If the window still doesn't appear, it may be positioned off-screen (see below)
    * To stop SGI from starting minimized, go to <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → General" /> and disable **Start minimized**
    * Can also happen if **WebView2** is missing or outdated. Download the "Evergreen Bootstrapper" via [Microsoft's WebView2 download page](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/) and relaunch SGI
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The window appears off-screen, too small, or in the wrong position" id="window-offscreen">
    SGI remembers its window size and position between sessions. If you changed monitor setups (e.g. disconnected a second monitor) the window may open off-screen.

    * Try pressing **Win + Shift + Left/Right Arrow** while the window is focused (use Alt+Tab to focus it) to move it back to your main display
    * Right-click the SGI taskbar icon and choose **Move** (or **Maximize**) if available
    * As a last resort, fully close SGI, delete `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\.window-state.json`, and relaunch. This resets the window to its default size and position
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="SGI starts but crashes or closes immediately" id="crash-on-start">
    * Check the most recent log file (in the `logs` folder next to where SGI stores its settings, see [Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug)) for the last recorded entries before the crash
    * Make sure your Windows is up to date. Tauri-based apps depend on the WebView2 runtime, which ships with Windows 10/11 but can be repaired via [Microsoft's WebView2 download page](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/) if missing or corrupted
    * If your settings file is corrupted, SGI may fail to start. Open the settings folder via <MockButton type="open-settings-file" /> in [Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug) (or `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\cache\` for an installed build) and rename or move `settings.json` elsewhere, then relaunch. SGI will recreate it with defaults
    * Try reinstalling the latest version
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Sign-In Issues [#sign-in-issues]
chunks.text:
Sign-In Issues [#sign-in-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="'Steam Sign-in' fails or gets stuck" id="agent-signin-stuck">
    * Make sure you have an active internet connection
    * Double check your username and password. If you're not sure, try signing in on [steamcommunity.com](https://steamcommunity.com/) directly first
    * If using the QR code, make sure you scanned it with the **Steam** mobile app's own QR scanner (top-right icon), not a generic QR app, and approve the prompt on your phone
    * An unscanned QR code expires after a short time and will automatically refresh itself, so there's no need to reopen the sign-in screen
    * Close the sign-in window and try again. It can occasionally get stuck on a stale attempt

    What each on-screen error means:

    * **"Incorrect username or password."** — self-explanatory; Steam doesn't distinguish a wrong username from a wrong password, so double-check both
    * **"Sign-in request denied in the Steam Mobile app. Please try again."** — appears when **Deny** is tapped (instead of **Approve**) for either a QR sign-in or a 2FA confirmation prompt. This is never auto-retried since it reflects a deliberate choice — just sign in again and tap **Approve** this time
    * **"Your Steam session isn't active anymore. Please sign in again."** or **"Your Steam ID hasn't been resolved yet. Please try again in a moment."** — usually transient, right after signing in or if the account was signed in elsewhere (see the "Signed in on another device" reconnect prompt). Wait a moment and retry
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="No Steam accounts show up on the Legacy Sign-in screen" id="no-accounts">
    Legacy Sign-in reads your locally saved Steam logins to populate the account picker.

    * Make sure the Steam client is installed and that you've logged in to your account(s) through Steam at least once

    * Open Steam and sign in normally, then restart SGI

    * If you use **Steam Guard**, complete the login fully (don't cancel at the 2FA prompt) before switching to SGI

    * If you'd rather not deal with the local Steam client at all, use [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) instead

    * **"Couldn't find a local Steam installation."** means SGI couldn't locate Steam at all — confirm it's actually installed

    * **"Couldn't read this device's saved Steam accounts."** means SGI found Steam but couldn't read its `loginusers.vdf` file. Signing in through the Steam client at least once (as above) regenerates this file
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Switching Legacy Sign-in accounts, or launching Steam from SGI, fails" id="legacy-account-switch-fails">
    These errors are all specific to **Legacy Sign-in**'s account switcher, which works by directly editing your local Steam client's saved login state:

    * **"That account could no longer be found."** — the account was removed from `loginusers.vdf` (e.g. it was signed out of the Steam client entirely) since SGI last read it. Sign in to it through Steam once more, then try switching again
    * **"Couldn't switch Steam accounts."** — SGI couldn't update the registry value Steam uses to decide which account to auto-login. Make sure Steam is fully closed before switching, and that SGI has normal write access to `HKEY_CURRENT_USER` (try running SGI as administrator once if this persists)
    * **"Couldn't start the Steam client."** — SGI couldn't launch `steam.exe`. Make sure Steam is installed in a standard location and isn't itself broken (try launching it manually)
    * **"Couldn't load account details right now."** — a transient failure fetching that account's profile summary from Steam. Retry, or check your internet connection
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A 'Steam is closed' warning appears while using SGI" id="steam-closed-warning">
    This only affects **Legacy Sign-in** accounts, which depend on the local Steam client staying open and signed in. If Steam closes, is restarted, or you sign out of it while SGI is running, any active idling/farming/unlocking for that account is stopped and this warning appears until Steam is running and signed in again.

    * Reopen the Steam client and make sure you're signed in to the same account
    * This doesn't affect [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) accounts, since they don't need a local Steam client at all

    You may also see this as **"Steam isn't running. Please start Steam and try again."** on a specific action (starting idling, unlocking an achievement, etc.) rather than as a standing banner — same cause, same fix.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Signed in, but my games list is empty or incomplete" id="empty-games-list">
    * Your Steam profile (or at least your **game details**) must be set to **Public** for SGI to read your library. Check this in your Steam profile's privacy settings
    * Try clicking <MockButton type="content" content="Refresh" /> on the <MockButton type="your-games" /> page
    * Try toggling **Settings → Debug → Clear Data** as a last resort if the cached games list is stuck (note this signs out every account and clears all local data)
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Idling Issues [#idling-issues]
chunks.text:
Idling Issues [#idling-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="A game won't start idling" id="idle-wont-start">
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, make sure the Steam client is running and you're signed in to the same account you're using in SGI
    * Make sure the game is actually owned on this account. SGI can't idle games you don't own
    * Check the log file (<MockButton type="view-log-file" /> in [Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug)) for a "Failed to start idling" message
    * If you recently reinstalled SGI, make sure `SteamUtility.exe` wasn't removed by your antivirus (see [Antivirus or Windows Defender is blocking SGI](#antivirus-blocking))
    * Close and reopen SGI, then try idling the game again

    If you see **"Couldn't start idling this game."**, this is the generic idle-start failure above — check the log file for the specific underlying reason (it's usually one of the causes listed here).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A game shows as idling in SGI but Steam doesn't show it as 'Currently in game'" id="idle-not-reflected">
    * Give it a minute, since there's a short delay before Steam's status updates
    * Make sure Steam itself is online (not in **Offline Mode**), as idling relies on Steam's servers being reachable
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, restarting Steam (not SGI) while a game is idling can desync the status. Stop and restart idling for that game
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Idling stops by itself" id="idle-stops">
    * Make sure your PC isn't going to sleep. Adjust Windows power settings so it stays awake while idling
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, Steam will stop "in-game" status if you launch the same game manually, or if Steam restarts/updates in the background
    * Check the log file for errors around the time idling stopped
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Leftover SteamUtility.exe processes after closing SGI or a crash" id="leftover-processes">
    If SGI is force-closed (e.g. via Task Manager, or a crash) before it can clean up, helper processes can be left running.

    * Open **Task Manager**, find any `SteamUtility.exe` entries, and select **End Task** for each
    * This won't affect your Steam library or achievements. It only stops the helper process
    * To avoid this in future, close SGI normally (via the tray menu **Quit** option) rather than force-closing it
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title=""This game has already reached its max playtime cap"" id="max-playtime-cap-reached">
    This is expected, not a bug. It means a **max playtime** limit is configured for this game (or for all games) under [Settings → Game Settings](/docs/settings/game-settings), and the game's total recorded playtime has already reached it. This cap applies everywhere a game can be idled — manual and automatic idling, the Achievement Unlocker, and Card Farming.

    * Raise or remove the max playtime limit in <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Game Settings" /> if you want to keep idling this game
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Free Games Issues [#free-games-issues]
chunks.text:
Free Games Issues [#free-games-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="`"Couldn't check Steam for free games right now"`" id="free-games-scrape-fails">
    This means SGI couldn't fetch or parse Steam's current free-games listings, which usually means Steam's storefront is temporarily unreachable or changed in a way SGI's scraper doesn't recognize yet.

    * Check your internet connection and try again in a few minutes
    * If this keeps happening across multiple sessions, it's worth reporting as a bug — see [Getting Help](#getting-help)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="`"Couldn't sign in/out of the Steam Store" (Gamer tier auto-redeem)`" id="free-games-store-signin-fails">
    Auto-redemption (Gamer tier) needs its own signed-in Steam Store session, separate from your SGI sign-in.

    * **"Couldn't sign in to the Steam Store. Please try again."** or **"Couldn't sign out of the Steam Store. Please try again."** — retry from <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Free Games" />. If it keeps failing, sign out and back in again to refresh the session
    * Manual claiming (the **Claim** button on the Free Games page) doesn't need this session and still works if auto-redeem is broken
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="`"Couldn't claim this game. It may no longer be free, or you may already own it"`" id="free-games-claim-fails">
    This isn't a bug — it means the claim itself was rejected by Steam, most commonly because:

    * The game stopped being free between SGI listing it and you clicking **Claim** (free-game promotions can end abruptly)
    * You already own the game on this account
    * Check your library to confirm — if the game is missing and still shows as free on Steam directly, try claiming again
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Card Farming & Inventory Manager Issues [#card-farming--inventory-manager-issues]
chunks.text:
Card Farming & Inventory Manager Issues [#card-farming--inventory-manager-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title=""Not logged in" or authentication errors" id="card-farming-not-logged-in">
    Card Farming and Inventory Manager rely on [Steam Credentials](/docs/steam-credentials), Steam Community session cookies which are separate from your SGI sign-in and expire periodically.

    * Go to **Settings → Steam Credentials** and re-authenticate (see the [Steam Credentials](/docs/steam-credentials) guide)
    * If you're on a **Gamer** tier account using **Steam Sign-in**, this normally happens automatically. Check that your subscription is still active
    * If you use **Family View** or have a **Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator**, make sure you complete the full login (these accounts often need the additional `steamMachineAuth` cookie)
    * Session cookies typically last a few hours to a few weeks. If farming worked before and suddenly stops with login errors, this is the most common cause

    On-screen error text and what it means:

    * **"Couldn't sign in to Steam Community. Check your cookies and try again."** — shown for a fresh cookie paste/connect attempt that didn't validate
    * **"Your Steam Community session has expired. Please reconnect to continue."** — shown when an already-working session stops working mid-farm/mid-session. Both point at the same fix above
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Family View is restricting Card Farming or Inventory Manager" id="family-view-restricted">
    If you see **"Family View is enabled on your Steam account. Disable Family View and try again."**, this is a different problem from the session/cookie errors above — your session cookies are genuinely valid, but Steam's Family View PIN gate is blocking this content class regardless. Reconnecting or re-pasting cookies will not fix this.

    * Open the Steam client, go to your account menu, and disable **Family View** (you'll need the Family View PIN)
    * Once disabled, Card Farming and Inventory Manager work normally again with no need to reconnect
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Card Farming isn't detecting card drops" id="card-farming-no-drops">
    * Make sure the games you're farming actually have **remaining card drops** for your account. Check your Badges page on Steam
    * Make sure your Steam profile's **game details/inventory** are set to Public
    * Re-authenticate if your session has expired (see above)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Listing cards on the Marketplace fails" id="market-listing-fails">
    * Make sure your Steam account doesn't have a **trade or market restriction** (new accounts, accounts without a phone number, or VAC-banned accounts can't use the Market)
    * Make sure you have **Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator** enabled for at least 7 days. Valve requires this for market access
    * If you're listing many items quickly, Steam may rate-limit you. Wait a few minutes and try again
    * Re-authenticate if your session cookies have expired
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Inventory Manager can't load items, prices, or listings" id="inventory-lookup-fails">
    A few distinct Inventory Manager errors, all usually transient Steam-side issues rather than something wrong with your account:

    * **"Couldn't load your Steam Community inventory right now."** / **"Couldn't fetch a market price right now."** / **"Couldn't read your active market listings."** — Steam Community was unreachable or returned an unexpected response. Wait a moment and retry
    * **"Steam is rate-limiting price lookups right now. Please try again in a moment."** — you've fetched too many item prices in a short time. This is separate from the Marketplace's own listing rate limit (see [Listing cards on the Marketplace fails](#market-listing-fails)) — wait a few minutes before fetching more prices
    * **"That item couldn't be found in your cached inventory."** — your local inventory cache is out of sync with Steam (e.g. the item was traded/sold elsewhere since the last refresh). Refresh your inventory to resync
    * **"Couldn't read or write the inventory cache."** — a local disk read/write failure. See [My settings reset, or SGI behaves like a fresh install](#settings-reset) for the same underlying cache-file pattern
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Achievement Manager & Unlocker Issues [#achievement-manager--unlocker-issues]
chunks.text:
Achievement Manager & Unlocker Issues [#achievement-manager--unlocker-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Achievements list is empty or won't load" id="achievements-empty">
    * Make sure the game actually has achievements (some games genuinely have none — SGI shows **"This app doesn't have achievement data."** in this case, which is expected, not a bug)
    * Try toggling the **refresh/refetch** option for that game to force SGI to re-fetch the achievement schema from Steam
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, make sure the Steam client is running and online
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Unlocking, locking, or toggling an achievement fails" id="achievement-toggle-fails">
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, make sure the Steam client is running and you're signed in to the matching account
    * Make sure the game isn't currently being idled by another tool, or already running through Steam itself, which can conflict with `SteamUtility.exe`
    * Check the log file for a specific error
    * Some games use **Family Sharing** or third-party anti-cheat that blocks stat writes. These games generally can't be modified

    On-screen error text and what it means:

    * **"That value is set by the game server and can't be changed."** — a genuinely different case from the Family Sharing one above. This achievement or statistic is flagged by the game itself as server-authoritative, so no client (SGI included) can write to it. This is a Steam-side restriction, not a bug
    * **"That achievement/statistic couldn't be found."** — usually a stale cached achievement schema. Try the refresh/refetch option above; if it still fails afterward, it's worth reporting
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title=""This game isn’t supported for achievements when signed in with Steam"" id="achievement-game-coordinator-unsupported">
    This is expected, not a bug. A small set of games (Team Fortress 2, Dota 2, CS2, Left 4 Dead 2, Portal 2) use Valve's Game Coordinator system for stats, which isn't reachable through **Steam Sign-in**'s architecture at all.

    * **On Windows**: switch to [Legacy Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#legacy-sign-in) for these specific games, which has no such restriction
    * **On Linux**: there's no local-client fallback (Legacy Sign-in doesn't exist on Linux), so these games can't be managed at all — this is a Steam architecture limitation, not something SGI can work around
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Achievement Unlocker isn't progressing" id="achievement-unlocker-stuck">
    * Make sure SGI is open (it can be minimized to tray, but not fully closed) for scheduled unlocking to continue
    * Check your unlock order, delay, and schedule settings under [Settings → Achievement Unlocker](/docs/settings/achievement-unlocker)
    * If you imported custom unlock timings, make sure the achievement names match exactly. See [Import Timings](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker/import-timings)
    * Check the log file for errors during the scheduled run
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Import Timings fails" id="import-timings-fails">
    [Import Timings](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker/import-timings) fetches another Steam profile's real unlock timestamps for a game, so its errors are about that target profile, not your own account or sign-in:

    * **"That profile is private or has no public achievement data."** — the profile you entered needs its game details/achievements set to public. Try a different profile, or ask that player to make theirs public temporarily
    * **"That player has no achievements with unlock timestamps for this game."** — the profile is public, but hasn't unlocked any achievements for this specific game
    * **"Couldn't resolve that profile."** — the SteamID64, profile URL, or vanity URL you entered couldn't be matched to a Steam account. Double-check it's correct
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Settings & Data Issues [#settings--data-issues]
chunks.text:
Settings & Data Issues [#settings--data-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="My settings reset, or SGI behaves like a fresh install" id="settings-reset">
    SGI stores app-wide settings in one `settings.json`, plus a separate file per feature (Achievement Unlocker, Card Farming, Inventory Manager, Free Games) for each signed-in Steam account. If any of these files becomes corrupted or unreadable, SGI falls back to that file's defaults automatically rather than failing to start.

    * Click <MockButton type="open-settings-file" /> in [Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug) to locate your settings folder
    * If you have a previously exported settings backup, re-import it (see [Export Settings](/docs/settings/debug#export-settings))
    * Switching accounts in SGI loads separate per-feature settings files for that account. This is expected, not a bug

    Any error mentioning it "couldn't read or write" a specific cache/settings file (games, favorites, automatic idler, achievement unlocker queue/settings/order, card farming, inventory manager, free games) follows this same self-healing pattern — SGI resets just that one file to defaults rather than failing to start.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Steam Web API key errors" id="api-key-errors">
    These appear when adding your own [Steam Web API key](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey) override under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → General" />:

    * **"Steam rejected that API key. Double-check it and try again."** — the key itself is invalid. Generate a fresh one from Steam and re-paste it
    * **"Couldn't access the Windows Credential Manager to store your API key."** — SGI couldn't save the key to your OS's secure credential store. This can happen if the credential store service isn't running, or (on Linux) if no keyring is set up — see [Sign-in fails or 'Your Steam session isn't active anymore' error](#linux-keyring-secret-service) for the same underlying fix
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Custom background image won't upload" id="background-image-invalid">
    **"That image couldn't be used - check the file type and size and try again."** means the file you picked under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Customization" /> failed validation.

    * Use a standard image format (PNG, JPG/JPEG, or WebP)
    * Try a smaller file if it's a very large/high-resolution image
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="License key won't activate" id="license-key-activation-fails">
    **"Couldn't activate this license key. Check that it's correct and try again."** means Steam Game Idler's licensing server rejected the key you entered under <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Subscription" />.

    * Double-check you copied the entire key with no extra spaces
    * Make sure you have an active internet connection
    * If the key was already active on another device, activating it here prompts a transfer confirmation instead of this error — this error means the key itself wasn't recognized
    * If you're confident the key is correct and this persists, see [Getting Help](#getting-help)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I fully reset SGI?" id="full-reset">
    <Steps>
      <Step>
        ### Try Reset Settings first [#try-reset-settings-first]

        Click <MockButton type="reset-settings" /> in <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Debug" />. This restores defaults without touching your games list or cached data
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Use Clear Data for a full wipe [#use-clear-data-for-a-full-wipe]

        Click <MockButton type="clear-data" /> in <MockButton type="context-cog" content="Settings → Debug" />. This removes all locally stored data and signs out every account

        <Callout type="warn">
          This is irreversible and will require you to sign in and reconfigure SGI again. Your Steam account and library are not affected.
        </Callout>
      </Step>

      <Step>
        ### Manual reset [#manual-reset]

        If SGI won't open at all, close it completely and delete the folder `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\`, then relaunch
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Update Issues [#update-issues]
chunks.text:
Update Issues [#update-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title=""Check for updates" does nothing, or no updates are found" id="update-check-nothing">
    * Make sure you have an active internet connection
    * SGI checks for updates via GitHub. If GitHub is unreachable from your network (e.g. blocked by a firewall/VPN), the check will fail silently
    * You can always download the latest release manually from the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases)
    * **Portable** builds don't support automatic updates. Download and replace the executable manually
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Update downloads but SGI doesn't restart, or restarts into the old version" id="update-stuck">
    * Manually close SGI completely (including from the system tray and Task Manager), then reopen it
    * If the version number still hasn't changed, uninstall and reinstall using the latest installer from GitHub
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — General Performance Issues [#general-performance-issues]
chunks.text:
General Performance Issues [#general-performance-issues]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="SGI is using high CPU or memory" id="high-cpu-memory">
    * If using **Legacy Sign-in**, idling many games simultaneously spawns a separate helper process per game. This is normal, but idling a very large number of games at once will increase resource usage. **Steam Sign-in** accounts idle through one shared session instead, which uses noticeably less
    * Check **Task Manager** to confirm whether the usage comes from `steam-game-idler.exe`, `SteamUtility.exe` or `webview2.exe` processes
    * Update to the latest version, as performance fixes are released regularly. See the [Changelog](/changelog)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="SGI feels slow or unresponsive" id="sgi-slow">
    * A large Steam library (thousands of games) can make initial loading slower. Give it a moment on first launch after sign-in
    * Running several **Steam Sign-in** accounts at once (see [Multi-Account](/docs/get-started/multi-account)) uses more memory and network than a single account. Reduce the number of concurrently signed-in accounts if resources are tight
    * Check the log file ([Debug Settings](/docs/settings/debug)) for repeated errors that may indicate a stuck background task
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Linux-Specific Notes [#linux-specific-notes]
chunks.text:
Linux-Specific Notes [#linux-specific-notes]


<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Which Linux install format should I use?" id="linux-which-format">
    `.deb` and `.rpm` are recommended — they run under native Wayland and don't have the AppImage's performance caveat below, plus they support the desktop's normal application launcher integration. The trade-off is no in-app automatic updates (see [Install](/docs/get-started/install#linux) for the full comparison). Use the AppImage if you want automatic updates, or if your distro doesn't provide a compatible `.deb`/`.rpm`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The AppImage feels slower or laggier than the .deb/.rpm install" id="linux-appimage-lag">
    This is expected, not a bug. The AppImage runs through a compatibility layer (XWayland) on a Wayland desktop, which has a real, hardware-independent performance cost. A `.deb`/`.rpm` install runs under native Wayland with no such layer. Switch to `.deb`/`.rpm` if this is noticeable for you.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A few visual quirks on Linux" id="linux-visual-quirks">
    A handful of small, cosmetic differences from Windows are known platform limitations, not bugs, and aren't fixable from SGI's side:

    * The window doesn't have rounded corners (Windows gets this from Windows 11's own window manager; Linux desktops have no equivalent for an undecorated window)
    * Left-clicking the tray icon always opens the tray menu instead of showing the window (a Linux tray-icon protocol limitation with no left/right-click distinction)
    * One extra click is sometimes needed after dragging the window by its titlebar (a currently-open upstream GTK issue)
    * An AppImage's taskbar/dock icon may show as generic instead of the SGI icon, even though the tray icon is correct — install via `.deb`/`.rpm` if this bothers you, since desktop icon integration is an AppImage ecosystem limitation, not something specific to SGI
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Missing dependency errors on install" id="linux-missing-deps">
    A `.deb`/`.rpm` install pulls in its required system libraries (WebKitGTK, GTK, `libayatana-appindicator3`, `libsecret`) automatically via your package manager. If you see a missing-dependency error anyway, make sure your package manager's repositories are up to date (`sudo apt update` / `sudo dnf check-update`) and try reinstalling. The AppImage bundles most of what it needs, so this shouldn't affect it.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Sign-in fails or 'Your Steam session isn't active anymore' error" id="linux-keyring-secret-service">
    SGI securely saves your session using your OS's built-in keyring. If your Linux setup doesn't have one running or SGI can't access it, you will need to fix this on your system, since SGI can't install or unlock it for you.

    * **GNOME desktops** (Ubuntu, Fedora Workstation, etc.): usually works automatically. If not, install it and log back in:
      ```bash
      sudo apt install gnome-keyring   # Ubuntu/Debian
      sudo dnf install gnome-keyring   # Fedora
      ```
    * **KDE Plasma desktops** (Kubuntu, Fedora KDE, etc.): go to **System Settings → KDE Wallet** and enable **"Enable the KDE Wallet subsystem"**
    * **Minimal desktops/tiling window managers** (Sway, i3, Hyprland, etc.): install it, then set it to start with your session — check your window manager's documentation for how to autostart it
      ```bash
      sudo pacman -S gnome-keyring   # Arch-based
      ```
    * **Bazzite and similar handheld/console distros**: sign in from **Desktop Mode**, not **Gaming Mode** — Gaming Mode's console-style session doesn't reliably support the keyring, which is a known limitation of that mode, not an SGI bug

    Already installed but still failing? It's likely locked or not running for your current session, rather than missing:

    * **GNOME**: open **Passwords and Keys** from your app menu. If the "Login" keyring shows a lock icon, click it and unlock with your password
    * **KDE Plasma**: open **KWallet Manager** (search "wallet" in your app menu) and unlock your wallet
    * **Auto-login users** (no password at your login screen): your keyring can't auto-unlock without a login password to unlock it with, so it stays locked every session. Unlock it manually as above each time, or open your keyring/wallet app and set it to use a blank password so it unlocks automatically
    * **Minimal desktops/tiling window managers**: if you just installed `gnome-keyring`, it still won't be running until your next login (or your session's autostart config is set up) — log out and back in, or start it once with `gnome-keyring-daemon --start --components=secrets` before relaunching SGI
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Where does SGI store its data on Linux?" id="linux-data-location">
    `~/.local/share/com.zevnda.steam-game-idler` — the equivalent of Windows' `%appdata%\com.zevnda.steam-game-idler\` referenced elsewhere on this page. The log file and settings file live there too, same structure as Windows.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

chunks.title: Troubleshooting — Getting Help [#getting-help]
chunks.text:
Getting Help [#getting-help]


<Callout type="info">
  Most errors show plain text like the ones quoted throughout this page. If you instead see a generic message like `Something went wrong... (some_error_code)` with a code that isn't mentioned anywhere on this page, it's likely an edge case SGI didn't anticipate rather than something you can fix yourself — please report it (include the code) rather than searching for a workaround
</Callout>

If these troubleshooting steps don't solve your issue:

1. **Check the [FAQ](/docs/faq)** for additional solutions
2. **Search existing issues** on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/issues)
3. **Create a new issue** with:
   * Detailed description of the problem
   * Steps to reproduce
   * Your system information (OS/version, Steam version)
   * Which sign-in method you're using (Steam Sign-in or Legacy Sign-in)
   * Relevant log file excerpts
   * Screenshots if applicable

<Callout type="info">
  When reporting issues, never share your Steam credentials or personal information
</Callout>

chunks.title: Build It Yourself — Build It Yourself [#build-it-yourself]
chunks.text:
Build It Yourself [#build-it-yourself]


SGI's source code is fully public on [GitHub](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler). The desktop app is a [Tauri](https://tauri.app/) app (Rust + Next.js), and it drives a bundled helper process, `SteamUtility`, built from a separate C#/.NET project at `libs/SteamUtility/`.

chunks.title: Build It Yourself — Prerequisites [#prerequisites]
chunks.text:
Prerequisites [#prerequisites]


* [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/prebuilt-installer) >= 20.0
* [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation) - the project uses pnpm workspaces, not npm/yarn
* [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) (stable toolchain)
* [.NET SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download) >= 8.0 (`libs/SteamUtility` targets `net8.0` only)

**Windows only:**

* [VS Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/) = latest, with the "Desktop development with C++" workload
* [WebView2](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/Microsoft-edge/webview2/) = latest (*pre-installed on Windows 11 and newer Windows 10 versions*)

**Linux only:**

* [Tauri's Linux prerequisite](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#linux) system dependencies for your distro

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Clone Repo [#clone-repo]

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler.git
    cd ./steam-game-idler
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install Dependencies [#install-dependencies]

    ```bash
    pnpm install
    ```

    This installs dependencies for both the root app and the `docs/` workspace package
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Build SteamUtility [#build-steamutility]

    ```bash
    dotnet build ./libs/SteamUtility/SteamUtility.csproj
    ```

    This outputs `SteamUtility` to `src-tauri/target/debug/libs/` (or `release/libs/` for a release build); `pnpm tauri dev`/`pnpm tauri build` expect it to already be there
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Create Environment Files [#create-environment-files]

    Create a `.env` file in the root of `./steam-game-idler` and add a `KEY` variable containing your [Steam Web API Key](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey)

    <Files>
      <Folder name="steam-game-idler">
        <Folder name="public" />

        <Folder name="libs" />

        <Folder name="docs" />

        <Folder name="src">
          <Folder name="pages" />

          <Folder name="features" />

          <Folder name="shared" />
        </Folder>

        <Folder name="src-tauri">
          <Folder name="tauri.conf.json" />
        </Folder>

        <File name=".env" className="bg-fd-primary/10 text-fd-primary hover:bg-fd-primary/20 hover:text-fd-primary" />

        <File name="pnpm-lock.yaml" />

        <File name="package.json" />
      </Folder>
    </Files>

    ```ini title=".env" copy
    KEY="ABC123******789XYZ"
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Development or Production Build [#development-or-production-build]

    ```bash
    # Development
    pnpm td       # shorthand for `tauri dev`

    # Production
    pnpm tb       # shorthand for `tauri build`, outputs to `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Build It Yourself — Other Useful Scripts [#other-useful-scripts]
chunks.text:
Other Useful Scripts [#other-useful-scripts]


Run these from the repo root:

| Script            | What it does                                         |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm typecheck`  | `tsc --noEmit` for the desktop app                   |
| `pnpm lint`       | ESLint for the desktop app                           |
| `pnpm dd`         | Starts the docs site dev server (this site)          |
| `pnpm build:docs` | Production build of the docs site                    |
| `pnpm build:libs` | Builds the `./libs/SteamUtility.csproj`              |
| `pnpm i18n:check` | Checks `en-US.json` for duplicate translation values |

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Install [#install]
chunks.text:
Install [#install]


SGI supports **Windows** (10/11, 64-bit) and **Linux** (64-bit). Follow the steps below for your OS and install method.

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Windows Installer [#windows-installer]
chunks.text:
Windows Installer [#windows-installer]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download]

    Download `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_x64-setup.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install [#install-1]

    Run the installer and follow the steps of the installation guide
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run]

    After installation, you can launch SGI in a few different ways:

    * Select "Run Steam Game Idler" and click "Finish" when prompted
    * Run `Steam Game Idler.exe` from the installation directory
      * Defaults to `C:/Program Files/Steam Game Idler`
    * Use the desktop shortcut created by the installer
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Windows Portable [#windows-portable]
chunks.text:
Windows Portable [#windows-portable]


<Callout type="warn">
  The portable version does not support automatic updates. You'll need to download and replace the executable manually for each new release
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download-1]

    Download `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_x64-portable.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Extract [#extract]

    Extract the contents of the `.zip` file to any folder you want
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run-1]

    Open the folder and run `Steam Game Idler.exe`
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Installation Guide — Linux [#linux]
chunks.text:
Linux [#linux]


<Callout type="info">
  Linux supports [Steam Sign-in](/docs/get-started/how-to-sign-in#steam-sign-in) only
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  SGI needs a working [OS keyring](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/secret-service/latest/) to securely store your session. This is preconfigured on most desktops, but if sign-in fails, or you get a "your Steam session isn't active anymore" error — see [this troubleshooting entry](/docs/troubleshooting#linux-keyring-secret-service)
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">
  The `.deb` / `.rpm` versions do not support automatic updates. You'll need to download and install the new package manually for each release
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Download [#download-2]

    Download the file matching your distro/format from the [latest release](https://github.com/zevnda/steam-game-idler/releases/latest/) page on GitHub:

    * **Debian/Ubuntu-based**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.deb`
    * **Fedora/openSUSE-based**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X-1.x86_64.rpm`
    * **Any distro**: `Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage`
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Install [#install-2]

    * **deb**:
      ```bash
      sudo dpkg -i Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.deb
      ```
    * **rpm**:
      ```bash
      sudo rpm -i Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X-1.x86_64.rpm
      ```
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Run [#run-2]

    * **deb/rpm**: launch SGI from your desktop's application launcher
    * **AppImage**: make it executable and run it directly
      ```bash
      chmod +x Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage
      ./Steam.Game.Idler_X.X.X_amd64.AppImage
      ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Manual Add — Manually Add a Game by App ID [#manually-add-a-game-by-app-id]
chunks.text:
Manually Add a Game by App ID [#manually-add-a-game-by-app-id]


Sometimes Steam or the app's developer removes a game from the Steam store entirely, and even though you still technically own it, it can no longer be found automatically. This feature is also useful for adding content like DLC, soundtracks, videos, and tools from your library that SGI doesn't automatically detect.

<Callout type="info">
  Manual Add doesn't verify the App ID against Steam. Double check the ID is correct by using a tool like [SteamDB](https://steamdb.info/).
</Callout>

chunks.title: Manual Add — Where It's Available [#where-its-available]
chunks.text:
Where It's Available [#where-its-available]


The <MockButton type="manual-add" /> button appears in the header of these pages:

* [Favorites](/docs/features/favorites)
* [Card Farming](/docs/features/card-farming)
* [Achievement Unlocker](/docs/features/achievement-unlocker)
* [Auto-Idle](/docs/features/auto-idle)

Each page adds the game to its own list only. For example, adding a game manually in Card Farming doesn't also add it to Favorites or Automatic Idler. Repeat the process on each page where you want it to appear.

chunks.title: Manual Add — Adding a Game [#adding-a-game]
chunks.text:
Adding a Game [#adding-a-game]


<Steps>
  <Step>
    Click the <MockButton type="manual-add" /> button in the top-right of the page header
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Enter a name for the game and its Steam App ID

    You can find a game's App ID in its Steam store URL, e.g. `store.steampowered.com/app/252950` has an App ID of `252950`. If the game is no longer available on the Steam store, you can use a tool like [SteamDB](https://steamdb.info/)
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Click <MockButton type="content" content="Add" /> to add it to the list
  </Step>

  <Step>
    Once a game has been added, you can right-click it to bring up a menu where you can idle it, view its achievements, and easily add it to other lists
  </Step>
</Steps>

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Account Switcher (Multi-Account)
chunks.text:
Account Switcher (Multi-Account)


This file is generated corpus content, produced by the `/generate-ui-guide` skill from the real
`src/features/account-switcher/` component source, its cross-feature store wiring, and the
`get-started/multi-account.mdx` docs page. It is the single merged source for this feature (UI +
docs + cross-feature connections) and should be regenerated via that skill whenever the account
switcher's UI, stores, or docs page change — not hand-patched for small drift. For the deeper "why"
behind multi-account behavior (not covered again here), see
`ai-corpus/architecture-guides/multi-account.md`.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Where the account switcher lives and how to open it
chunks.text:
Where the account switcher lives and how to open it


The account switcher is permanent app chrome, not a page of its own — it has no route under
`/dashboard/*`. It's rendered by `Sidebar.tsx` as part of a "Discord-style user bar" fixed at the
bottom of the sidebar, right next to the Settings gear icon button (`TbSettings`, opens the
Settings modal to whatever tab was last active). This bar is the app's one sign-out entry point —
there is no separate standalone "sign out" button anywhere else in the app.

- **Expanded sidebar**: the trigger is a full-width row showing your avatar (`Avatar`, falling back
  to your display name's first letter in a circle if no avatar has loaded yet), your current
  account's display name (Steam persona name once resolved, otherwise the raw sign-in identifier —
  your Steam username for a Steam Sign-in account, or your SteamID64 for a Legacy Sign-in account),
  and a chevron-down icon (`TbChevronDown`) on the far right.
- **Collapsed sidebar** (icon-rail mode, toggled by Ctrl+W): the trigger shrinks to just the avatar,
  with the account name moved into a hover tooltip instead (delay 300ms, appears to the right of
  the icon). This is driven by the switcher's own `compact` prop, which `Sidebar.tsx` sets from
  `sidebarStore`'s collapsed state.

Clicking the trigger opens a popover (anchored above the trigger, `placement='top'`) containing:
one row per signed-in account, a horizontal divider, and an "Add another account" row at the
bottom. The popover is implemented with HeroUI's `Popover` (not `Dropdown`/`Menu`) specifically
because each account row needs its own nested interactive sign-out button, which would conflict
with `Menu`'s item click semantics in react-aria-components.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — The account list — one row per signed-in account
chunks.text:
The account list — one row per signed-in account


Every account you've signed into and haven't explicitly signed out of gets a row, sourced from
`sessionStore`'s `accounts: Record<AccountKey, SignedInAccount>` map (`AccountKey` is
`"agent:<username>"` for a Steam Sign-in account or `"local:<steamId>"` for a Legacy Sign-in
account). Each row shows:

- **Avatar** (small, left) with a fallback initial letter if no avatar summary has resolved yet.
- **Display name** (Steam persona name if resolved via `accountSummaryStore`, otherwise the raw
  username/SteamID64), truncated with an ellipsis if too long for the row.
- **Mode label** underneath the name, in small muted text: "Signed in with Steam" for a Steam
  Sign-in (agent-mode) account, or "Local Steam client" for a Legacy Sign-in (CLI-mode) account —
  these are the literal `dashboard.sidebar.accountSwitcher.modeAgent`/`modeLocal` strings. Note this
  differs from the sign-in button labels themselves ("Steam Sign-in" / "Legacy Sign-in", used on the
  sign-in landing screen) — same two modes, different label wording depending on where in the UI
  you're looking.
- **A small filled dot** (accent color, bottom-right corner of the avatar) if that account currently
  has *any* automation running — idling, card farming, or achievement unlocking — regardless of
  whether that account is the one currently active/displayed. This is the "automation running"
  indicator described in the cross-feature section below.
- **The active account's row** is highlighted with a soft accent background (`bg-accent-soft`).
- **A sign-out button** on the far right of each row: a logout icon (`TbLogout`), `aria-label` "Sign
  out of {displayName}". Clicking it never triggers a switch — it calls `event.stopPropagation()`
  and always opens the sign-out flow described below, even for a row that isn't the active account.
- While a row is mid-switch (see below), its sign-out button is replaced by a small spinner, and the
  whole row becomes visually dimmed (70% opacity) and non-interactive until the switch finishes.

Clicking anywhere on a row *other than* the sign-out button attempts to switch to that account
(unless the row needs special handling — see the over-cap and reauth states below). Clicking the
already-active row's body does nothing (no-op).

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Switching accounts
chunks.text:
Switching accounts


Clicking a normal, in-good-standing row that isn't already active calls `switchAccount(key)` on
`sessionStore`, which updates `activeAccountKey` and the denormalized `account` field, and persists
the new active key to `localStorage` so it's remembered across app restarts.

- **Local (Legacy Sign-in) accounts get a pre-flight check**: before switching, the app calls the
  `is_steam_running` command. If the local Steam client isn't running, the switch is aborted, a
  warning toast fires ("Steam needs to be running to switch to this account"), and the app's
  persistent Steam-down warning modal is raised (via `steamWarningStore`). This exists because a
  Legacy Sign-in account can't do anything without a real, running local Steam client — silently
  switching into it anyway would land you on an account that can't function.
- **Steam Sign-in (agent-mode) accounts switch immediately**, no pre-flight check.
- On a successful switch: any active search query is cleared (a search scoped to the previous
  account's owned games/achievements/cards is stale for the new account), an info toast fires
  ("Switched to {name}"), and the app navigates to `/dashboard` (the Games page) regardless of which
  page you were on — a page scoped to the old account's data (e.g. a card-farming run in progress
  view) has no meaning for the newly active account.
- While a switch is in flight, that specific row shows a spinner in place of its sign-out button and
  becomes non-interactive; further clicks on it are ignored until the switch completes.
- The popover closes automatically once the switch finishes.

Every added account keeps running its own idling, card farming, and achievement-unlocking
independently in the background regardless of which account is currently active/displayed —
switching only changes which account's dashboard you're looking at, it never pauses anything.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Adding another account
chunks.text:
Adding another account


The "Add another account" row sits below the divider at the bottom of the account list popover: a
plus icon (`TbPlus`) plus the text "Add another account" (`dashboard.sidebar.accountSwitcher.
addAccount.trigger`). Clicking it closes the popover and opens `AddAccountModal` (driven by
`addAccountModalStore`, rendered once in `DashboardShell`).

`AddAccountModal` reuses the exact same building blocks as the app's initial sign-in flow —
`SignInLanding` (the same landing card with "Steam Sign-in" and "Legacy Sign-in" buttons),
`CredentialsForm`/`GuardCodeForm`/`QrSignInPanel` for the Steam Sign-in path, and `AccountPicker`
for the Legacy Sign-in path — completely unmodified except for a few new props passed only when
embedded this way. The full click-by-click detail of those sign-in forms themselves lives in the
sign-in-landing/agent-sign-in/local-sign-in guides, not repeated here; this section only covers what
changes about that flow when it's reached through "Add another account" instead of the initial
sign-in screen:

- **The Terms of Service / Privacy Policy acknowledgment footer is hidden** (`embedded` prop) — that
  acknowledgment only makes sense once, at the very first sign-in.
- **The credentials form and the QR panel are stacked vertically** (credentials above a divider
  above the QR panel), rather than the standalone sign-in screen's side-by-side two-column layout —
  the modal is a narrower, vertical context.
- **Legacy Sign-in is disabled with a native disabled button** if a Legacy Sign-in account is already
  signed in ("A local Steam client account is already signed in — only one can be signed in at a
  time."). This is a real, non-monetization technical ceiling (a real local Steam client can only be
  logged into one account at all), so unlike every tier gate in this app, it correctly uses a native
  `isDisabled` button rather than the pressable-with-badge pattern.
- **Steam Sign-in can be gated by the concurrent-account tier cap**, in one of two distinct ways:
  - If you're already on Gamer tier and have hit its own sanity-capped ceiling of 10 concurrent
    Steam Sign-in accounts, the "Steam Sign-in" button becomes a genuine native-disabled button (no
    upgrade would help), with muted helper text below it: "You've reached the maximum number of
    accounts that can be signed in with Steam at the same time."
  - If you're on Free or Casual and have hit your tier's lower cap (1 for Free, 3 for Casual), the
    button instead stays a real, clickable, dimmed-looking (50% opacity) button with a "GAMER"
    `TierBadge` next to its label, and clicking it opens the upgrade modal (`GoProModal`, pre-scrolled
    to the Gamer tier) instead of starting sign-in — the standard tier-gating pattern used everywhere
    else in this app (never a swallowed click). The helper text below reads: "The {tier} plan allows
    {count} account(s) signed in with Steam at a time. Sign out of one to add another, or upgrade for
    more." — where `{tier}` is "Casual" or "Free" and `{count}` is 1 or 3.
- On success, the modal shows a centered loading spinner, then closes itself, shows a success toast
  ("Added {name}"), and navigates to `/dashboard` — mirroring the account-switcher's own post-switch
  toast/navigation behavior. The newly added account automatically becomes the active account (its
  sign-in hook already made it active internally before this fires), so the toast/navigation reflect
  it, not whatever account was active before.

**Concurrent account caps** (Steam Sign-in only — a Legacy Sign-in account never counts against
this): Free allows 1, Casual allows up to 3, Gamer allows up to 10 concurrent Steam Sign-in
accounts. You can additionally always have one Legacy Sign-in account signed in alongside any number
of Steam Sign-in accounts, at any tier — Legacy Sign-in doesn't count against the cap at all, since
its one-account ceiling is a real Steam-client constraint, not a subscription tier.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Signing out
chunks.text:
Signing out


Every row's sign-out button (the `TbLogout` icon, far right) is the app's one sign-out entry point
for that account, whether or not it's the currently active one.

- **If that account has no automation currently running** (no idling, card farming, or achievement
  unlocking in progress), clicking sign-out signs it out immediately with no confirmation.
- **If that account has automation running**, clicking sign-out instead closes the popover and opens
  a confirmation dialog (`AlertDialog`) titled "Sign out?" with the description: "This will stop the
  automation currently running for {name} and sign that account out." It has a "Cancel" button
  (secondary style) and a "Sign out" button (danger/red style, shows a pending spinner while sign-out
  is in progress). This is the one sign-out consequence considered worth pausing for — everything
  else about sign-out is instant.
- Signing out an account stops its card farming and achievement unlocker first, then either logs the
  agent-mode session off cleanly (`agent_logout`) or, for a Legacy Sign-in account, stops its idling
  processes (`stop_all_idling`) — both scoped to just that one account. Only that account's cached
  idling/games/card-farming/achievement-unlocker/summary state is cleared; every other signed-in
  account's cached state is left untouched.
- **The blanket `kill_all_steam_utility_processes` command is never called while any other account
  remains signed in** — it only fires as a last-resort cleanup once the account you just signed out
  was the *last* one signed in at all (i.e., you're now fully signed out of the app). Calling it
  earlier would kill every other concurrently signed-in account's process too.
- If signing out the account leaves zero accounts signed in, the app navigates back to the sign-in
  landing page (`/`).
- If you signed out the *active* account but other accounts remain, the app auto-switches to
  whichever account is now active (picked automatically by `sessionStore`) and shows the same
  "Switched to {name}" toast a normal switch would show — from your perspective this is still a
  switch, just one you didn't explicitly pick a target for.
- If the cleanup itself partially fails (e.g. the stop-automation calls or the logout call errors),
  you still get signed out, but see an additional danger toast: "Sign-out cleanup didn't fully
  finish, but you've been signed out."

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Accounts over the concurrent-account cap (subscription downgrade)
chunks.text:
Accounts over the concurrent-account cap (subscription downgrade)


If your subscription lapses or you downgrade to a lower tier while you have more Steam Sign-in
accounts signed in than the new tier allows, **the app never force-signs-out any account over the
cap** — this is a deliberate, absolute rule; only an explicit sign-out action (above) ever stops an
account's automation. Instead:

- Every over-cap account's row in the switcher stays visible but visually dimmed (50% opacity on
  both the avatar and the name/mode-label block), and shows a "GAMER" `TierBadge` next to its mode
  label.
- Clicking an over-cap row does not switch to it — it closes the popover and opens the upgrade modal
  (`GoProModal`, pre-scrolled to Gamer tier) instead.
- The over-cap row's sign-out button remains fully functional and untouched by any of this — you can
  always sign an over-cap account out directly from its row exactly as described above.
- If the account that was *active* at the moment of a downgrade becomes over-cap, the app
  automatically falls back to switching the active account to the very first account you ever added
  (which is always allowed under any tier, since every tier's cap is at least 1) — this prevents you
  from being stranded on a now-locked account with no visible way back except manually reopening the
  switcher.
- Being over-cap doesn't stop that account's backend automation from running if it was already
  running before the downgrade — the cap only blocks new switches to it, and its automation keeps
  running invisibly in the background even while its row is dimmed, until you either upgrade again or
  explicitly sign it out.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — "Signed in elsewhere" — the reconnect/reauth flow
chunks.text:
"Signed in elsewhere" — the reconnect/reauth flow


If a Steam Sign-in account gets signed in on another device or session (Steam only allows one active
session per account for this sign-in method), the app detects this automatically and reacts even if
the account switcher popover isn't open:

- A red-tinted badge appears on that account's row: a warning-triangle icon (`TbAlertTriangle`) plus
  the text "Signed in elsewhere", with a tooltip on hover: "This account was signed in on another
  device, so its automation has been paused. Sign in again to continue."
- `ReauthModal` (driven by `reauthModalStore`, rendered once in `DashboardShell`) **opens
  automatically the instant this is detected**, without you needing to click anything — a badge alone
  was found to be too easy to miss for something this disruptive. No separate toast fires for this;
  the modal opening is itself the notification.
- By the time this badge/modal appears, that account's card farming and achievement unlocking have
  already been stopped on the backend.
- Clicking a reauth-flagged row directly in the switcher (instead of waiting for the automatic popup)
  reopens the same `ReauthModal` for that account.
- **`ReauthModal`'s content**: title "Signed in on another device", body text "{account} was signed
  in on another device, so its automation has been paused. Sign in again to continue.", followed by a
  second line explaining the underlying limitation: "Steam Sign-in only allows one active session per
  account. If you'd like to keep playing games while Steam Game Idler runs, use Legacy Sign-in
  instead." Two buttons:
  - **"Reconnect"** (primary) — attempts to resume the same account's session using its saved
    refresh token (`agent_login_with_token`), the same mechanism used to silently resume accounts on
    app launch. It does *not* ask for a password again. If this succeeds, the modal closes and the
    reauth badge clears itself once the daemon's next status event confirms the reconnect (not
    immediately on click). If it fails, an inline red alert shows an error message beneath the
    buttons; if there's no saved credential left to reconnect with at all, the modal automatically
    falls through to the "use a different sign-in method" flow below instead of just showing an
    error.
  - **"Use a different sign-in method"** (secondary) — closes `ReauthModal` and opens the same
    `AddAccountModal` flow "+ Add another account" uses. This is the only path back to a genuinely
    different sign-in mode (e.g. switching that same account over to Legacy Sign-in) — the reauth
    flow itself never offers a password-entry form of its own.
- The reauth-needed state (`isOverCap`'s sibling flag on each row) takes priority over the over-cap
  dimmed state if a row is somehow both — a reauth-needed account has already had its automation
  stopped and genuinely needs fresh credentials before anything else about it applies, whereas an
  over-cap account is still a normal, live session that's merely not switchable.

chunks.title: Account Switcher (Multi-Account) — Cross-feature connections
chunks.text:
Cross-feature connections


- **`sessionStore`** (`src/shared/stores/sessionStore.ts`) is what the switcher's account list is
  built from directly: `accounts: Record<AccountKey, SignedInAccount>` for every row, and
  `activeAccountKey`/`account` for which row is highlighted and what "switch"/"sign out" acts on by
  default. Nearly every other feature in the app also reads this store to know which account to
  query.
- **Per-account automation dot reads other features' stores directly, not their denormalized view.**
  The switcher reads `idlingStore.entries[accountKey]?.appIds.length`,
  `cardFarmingStore.entries[accountKey]?.isFarming`, and
  `achievementUnlockerStore.entries[accountKey]?.isRunning` — the raw per-account `entries` map each
  of those stores keeps, not the single "currently active account" denormalized field those stores
  also expose. This is deliberate: a *backgrounded* account's automation state has to stay observable
  in the switcher even while a different account is the one actively displayed, which the
  denormalized view (scoped to only the active account) can't provide.
- **`accountSummaryStore`** supplies each row's resolved persona name/avatar, keyed by `AccountKey` —
  until it resolves for a given account, the row falls back to the raw sign-in identifier
  (username/SteamID64) and an initial-letter avatar.
- **`subscriptionStore`** (via `computeAllowedAccountKeys`/`maxConcurrentAgentAccounts` in
  `subscriptionAccess.ts`) drives which rows are dimmed/over-cap and what `AddAccountModal`'s Steam
  Sign-in button does when the cap is hit.
- **`proModalStore`**'s `openWithTier('gamer')` is what both the over-cap row click and
  `AddAccountModal`'s upsell button reroute to — the shared tier-gating pattern used throughout the
  app: a gated control always stays a real, clickable element (never native-`isDisabled`) with a
  `TierBadge`, rerouted to open the upgrade modal instead of performing the real action.
- **`searchStore.clearAllQueries()`** is called on both a successful switch and a sign-out that
  affected the active account — any in-flight search is scoped to the previous account's data and
  would otherwise show stale results after the switch.
- **Sign-out clears exactly one account's entry** from `idlingStore`, `gamesListStore`,
  `cardFarmingStore`, `achievementUnlockerStore`, and `accountSummaryStore` (each store's
  `clearEntry`/`clearSummary`), then `sessionStore.clearAccount(key)` — never a blanket reset of
  these stores, so other signed-in accounts' cached data survives.
- **`steamWarningStore`** is raised by a failed `is_steam_running` pre-flight check when switching
  into a Legacy Sign-in account while the local Steam client isn't running.
- **`useAgentAccountCapEnforcement`** and **`useAgentReauthWatcher`** (both mounted once in
  `DashboardShell`, not owned by the switcher's own components) are what actually drive the
  over-cap-fallback-switch and the automatic `ReauthModal` pop-open described above — the switcher's
  own components only render the resulting state, they don't detect these conditions themselves.
- **Settings**: the account switcher itself has no dedicated Settings tab or settings file of its
  own — account data lives in `sessionStore`'s `localStorage`-persisted session blob (candidate-only,
  re-validated against the real backend on every app launch by `useSessionBootstrap`, never blindly
  trusted) plus each agent-mode account's refresh token in the OS credential store (Windows
